title: Company-wide policies and processes: Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Asha Kapoor
summary: Master reference for company-wide policies and operational processes covering access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding and management, travel rules, and canonical internal templates.
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for the most common cross-functional processes. It is intended as the single source of truth for employees and managers to understand required controls, approvers, SLAs, and where to find canonical templates.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors that interact with company systems, data, or facilities.

Contains sections for: Access & Permissions, Change Management, Data Management, Procurement & Expenses, Vendor Management, Travel Policies, and Internal Templates.

Owners & Contacts

- Document owner: People Ops (owner_team)
- Security contact: Platform Security (security-team@redwood-inference.internal)
- Procurement: Finance & Procurement (procurement@redwood-inference.internal)
- Vendor intake: Vendor Ops (vendor-ops@redwood-inference.internal)

1) Access & Permissions

Purpose
Ensure least-privilege access, timely provisioning/deprovisioning, auditable approvals, and regular access reviews.

Roles & Access Levels
- Org Admin: full control over org-level settings and billing. Very limited population, requires exec approval.
- System Owner / App Admin: manage service-level access and config.
- Engineer (Write): development and deployment privileges for designated services.
- Analyst (Read / Query): access to product analytics, dashboards.
- Contractor / Temporary: time-bound access with automatic expiry.

Provisioning Process (standard request)
1. Submit access request via Access Portal (Okta self-service) with justification and approver (manager or system owner).
2. Manager approval required for any Write-level access; System Owner approval required for privileged roles.
3. Access granted by IAM team and ticket created in Jira tagged "access-grant". SLA: 48 business hours for standard requests.

Emergency (break-glass) access
- Use BreakGlass flow in the Access Portal with mandatory justification and ticket.
- Emergency access expires after 4 hours unless extended with additional approvals.
- All break-glass sessions are logged and subject to immediate audit.

Deprovisioning
- On offboarding, managers must complete the offboarding checklist in People Ops. Deprovisioning of org and service access must be completed within 24 hours of the employee's termination date.
- Contractors: access auto-expires on contract end date; renewal requires re-approval.

Periodic Reviews
- Quarterly access reviews for all privileged roles.
- System owners must attest to access lists within 10 business days of review request.

MFA & Device Controls
- MFA required for all accounts with access to internal systems.
- Company-managed devices must have disk encryption, EDR agent, and pass baseline patching policy.

2) Change Management

Purpose
Minimize production risk while enabling predictable delivery. Maintain clear audit trails and rollback plans.

Change types
- Standard: Pre-authorized, repeatable changes (scheduled config updates, certificate renewals). No CAB approval required but must follow checklist.
- Normal: Non-routine changes that require change ticket, risk assessment, testing, and CAB approval.
- Emergency: Patches/fixes required to address production incidents. Emergency CAB meets ad-hoc; post-facto review required.

Workflow (normal change)
1. Create Change Request in Change Management system (Jira project: INFRA-CHANGE) with: description, affected services, rollback plan, test plan, scheduled window, and owner.
2. Risk assessment and pre-implementation checklist completed by owner.
3. Submit to Change Advisory Board (CAB) for approval. CAB meets weekly; for high-risk items expedite route available.
4. Implement during approved window; execution recorded in ticket.
5. Post-change verification and closure.

Approval thresholds
- Routine app config/infra: Team lead approval.
- Service-impacting changes (customer-facing or > 15 mins downtime risk): Director-level + CAB approval.
- Architectural or cross-service changes: VP or above + CAB.

Testing & Rollback
- All normal changes must include a rollback plan and a backout checklist.
- For database migrations, include dry-run plan and backup snapshot (point-in-time) details.

Communications
- Change owner must notify affected customers/teams 48 hours prior for any customer-impacting change.

3) Data Management

Purpose
Protect data confidentiality, integrity, and availability while enabling productive use.

Classification
- Public: Can be published externally.
- Internal: Company-internal information; not for public distribution.
- Restricted: Business-sensitive data (customer lists, pricing). Requires ACL controls and audit logging.
- Confidential / PII: Personal data, regulated data. Stronger controls, encryption, and access monitoring.

Storage & Encryption
- All production data must be encrypted at rest (KMS-managed) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Encryption keys for customer-sensitive data must be managed in KMS with restricted access.

Retention & Deletion
- Default retention: logs 90 days, analytics aggregates 2 years, backups 90 days unless otherwise specified.
- PII retention must follow legal/regulatory retention schedules; data deletion requests (subject access / erasure) must be acknowledged within 5 business days and completed within 30 calendar days unless legal hold applies.

Backups & DR
- Production backups: daily snapshots with at least 30-day retention for user-facing databases.
- DR exercise: annual full recovery test for core services (runtime, auth, billing).

Access Controls & Monitoring
- Principle of least privilege enforced via IAM groups and role-based policies.
- DLP scanning applied to attachments and file shares when possible.
- Sensitive data access must be logged and audited quarterly.

Data Transfers & Third Parties
- Transfers of restricted/confidential data to third parties require a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and a documented security review.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Purpose
Ensure fiscal controls, consistent vendor engagement, and transparent expense reimbursement.

Procurement process
1. Create a Purchase Requisition in the Procurement Portal with business justification and estimated cost.
2. Manager approval required for requisitions up to $5,000. Finance approval required for $5,001-$25,000. Legal & Procurement review required for >$25,000.
3. Procurement team issues PO and manages vendor contract signature.

PO & Contracting
- No vendor work should begin without an approved PO or signed contract unless pre-approved by Procurement.
- Contracts with data access require security review and standard data protection addenda.

Expense policy (employee reimbursable items)
- Employees should submit expenses in Expensify within 30 days of expense.
- Per diem: $75 domestic daily for meals; actual lodging reimbursed with receipts up to reasonable rate set by Finance.
- Manager approval required for expenses; Finance conducts monthly audits.
- Corporate card: only for business travel and pre-approved purchases; lost card must be reported immediately to Finance.

Approval matrix (summary)
- Manager: up to $1,000 for discretionary spend.
- Director: up to $10,000.
- Finance Director: up to $25,000.
- CFO: > $25,000 or strategic vendor relationships.

5) Vendor Management

Purpose
Onboard and manage third parties to minimize business and security risk.

Onboarding checklist
- Business case and sponsor identified.
- Procurement requisition created and approved.
- Legal review and executed contract (NDA, Master Services Agreement, DPA if applicable).
- Security review: vendor questionnaire, SOC2 / ISO reports reviewed as relevant.
- Technical onboarding plan and least-privilege access provisioning.

Security & Compliance requirements
- Vendors with access to confidential data must provide latest SOC2/ISO report or complete the Redwood security questionnaire.
- For high-risk vendors, require penetration test results or onsite security assessment.

Ongoing vendor governance
- Annual vendor reviews for high-impact vendors (financial, customer data access, production dependencies).
- Maintain vendor inventory with risk ratings and contract renewal reminders.

Termination
- Offboarding checklist includes access revocation, return/secure destruction of data, and confirmation of final invoices.

6) Travel Policies

Booking & Approvals
- All travel must be booked through the approved corporate travel tool (Concur).
- Travel requests require manager approval at least 5 business days prior to travel. International travel requires People Ops notification and a security briefing for destinations flagged as medium/high risk.

Reimbursement & Per Diem
- Submit receipts in Expensify within 30 days.
- Meal per diem: $75 domestic; rates for international per Finance table.
- Ground transportation: use approved vendors (rideshare, approved car services).

Safety & Insurance
- Company travel insurance covers business travel; employee must carry proof of coverage.
- For high-risk travel, employee must register itinerary with People Ops and Procurement will arrange additional security support if required.

7) Internal Templates & Canonical Forms

Canonical templates are available in the Templates repository (Confluence attachments and shared drive). Key templates include:
- Purchase Order (PO) template
- Vendor Security Questionnaire
- Data Classification Matrix
- Change Request template (INFRA-CHANGE)
- Offboarding & Access Revocation checklist
- Travel Request form
- Expense Reimbursement checklist

How to use templates
- Always use the latest template version; template versioning is tracked in the Templates repository.
- When deviating from a template for legal or regulatory reasons, attach an exception request and obtain approvals from People Ops and Legal.

Compliance, Audits & Exceptions

Audit readiness
- Maintain documentation for procurement, vendor security reviews, and change tickets for audit cycles.
- Each system owner is responsible for producing evidence for access reviews and change approvals when requested by Internal Audit.

Exceptions
- Exceptions to these policies require a documented risk assessment and approval by the designated approver (People Ops for HR-related exceptions, Security for data or access exceptions, Finance for procurement exceptions).

Appendix A \u2014 Quick checklists (copyable)

Access request checklist:
1. Business justification
2. Manager approver
3. System owner approver (if privileged)
4. Requested access duration

Change checklist (pre-implementation):
1. Backout plan in ticket
2. Snapshot / backup verified
3. Testing completed in staging
4. Communications ready

Vendor onboarding checklist (summary):
1. Requisition & PO/contract
2. Security questionnaire / SOC2
3. Technical onboarding plan
4. Access & monitoring configured
